title: LLMs’ Reading Comprehension Is Affected by Parametric Knowledge and Struggles with Hypothetical Statements
extended_summary:
This paper examines a fundamental evaluation problem in large language model (LLM) reading comprehension: when models answer questions from a text prompt, their responses can be influenced by parametric knowledge acquired during pretraining rather than by the provided context. The authors argue that this makes standard reading-comprehension evaluation misleading, because a correct answer may reflect memorized world knowledge rather than actual text understanding.

To address this, they propose an evaluation framework based on "imaginary" reading-comprehension instances, in which real-world entities and facts are replaced with fictitious ones so that the examples neither match nor contradict the models’ internal knowledge. They test multiple LLMs, including GPT-3.5, GPT-4, LLaMA 2, and Mixtral, on extractive QA tasks with supported, contradicting, and imaginary contexts. They then extend the benchmark to non-affirmative constructions such as negation, negative non-factives, modals, and conditionals to see whether models can correctly abstain when the text does not answer the question.

The results show that performance on ordinary affirmative contexts can be inflated or distorted by knowledge alignment/conflict effects. Across models, hypothetical constructions, especially modals and conditionals, are much harder than simple affirmatives or negations, and they also trigger stronger susceptibility to knowledge conflicts. The paper concludes that LLMs are not reliably context-faithful, particularly for semantically complex or hypothetical text, and that evaluation of text understanding should use imaginary data to separate linguistic comprehension from memorized knowledge.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI GPT-family chat-based large language models used for zero-shot question answering and extractive reading comprehension.
identified_tools.use_case: Evaluated as ChatGPT/GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 models on imaginary, supported, and contradicting reading-comprehension contexts to test context-faithfulness and handling of non-affirmative statements; also used in prompt-mitigation experiments.

findings.finding_summary: Across supported affirmative QA, models achieved near-perfect F1 on the supported set, but performance dropped on contradicting contexts (first GPT-4 prompt and both GPT-3.5 prompts fell below 70% F1). On the imaginary set, performance was near-perfect, indicating that the apparent supported-set success may be inflated by parametric knowledge rather than text understanding.
findings.measure: SQuAD F1 on supported, contradicting, and imaginary context-question pairs

findings.finding_summary: On non-affirmative imaginary contexts (negation, unlikely, modals, conditionals), ChatGPT showed a pronounced performance drop for hypotheticals, especially modals and conditionals, and often failed to abstain. Manual error analysis found that 94.64% of errors involved ignoring entailment-cancelling modifications and answering as if the context were affirmative.
findings.measure: F1 on non-affirmative imaginary benchmark; manual error analysis of errors

findings.finding_summary: In re-assessing context-faithfulness, ChatGPT was often affected by knowledge conflicts: supported contexts tended to suppress abstention and contradicting contexts often triggered abstention, especially for hypotheticals. Prompting strategies improved average performance but did not eliminate the gap; instructed prompting and two-step prompting helped most, while chain-of-thought was inconsistent across non-affirmative sets.
findings.measure: Average non-affirmative performance across supported, contradicting, and imaginary sets under different prompts
findings.sample_size: n=50 per condition; 2880 manually analyzed responses

identified_tools.name: LLaMA
identified_tools.description: Meta LLaMA-family large language models used here as zero-shot extractive QA systems.
identified_tools.use_case: Evaluated in LLaMA 2 chat form on the same reading-comprehension benchmarks to test text understanding, abstention, and susceptibility to knowledge conflicts.

findings.finding_summary: LLaMA 2 achieved near-perfect performance on supported affirmative items and near-perfect performance on the imaginary set, but was vulnerable to knowledge-conflict effects on contradicting contexts. On non-affirmative contexts, it handled simple negation relatively well but showed much weaker performance on modals and conditionals, with the largest gaps between supported, imaginary, and contradicting sets among the more semantically complex cases.
findings.measure: SQuAD F1 on supported, contradicting, and imaginary context-question pairs; non-affirmative F1 by semantic condition

findings.finding_summary: In context-faithfulness tests, LLaMA 2 was noted as an exception among models on hypothetical contexts: contradicting-set performance was not higher than imaginary-set performance and was sometimes lower. Manual inspection suggested that LLaMA 2 more often produced parametric answers instead of abstaining, which reduced performance on contradicting data.
findings.measure: Relative performance across supported, contradicting, and imaginary sets; manual error analysis
findings.sample_size: n=50 per condition; 2880 manually analyzed responses

identified_tools.name: Mistral
identified_tools.description: Mistral AI large language model used as a zero-shot extractive QA system.
identified_tools.use_case: Evaluated as Mixtral 8x7B Instruct on reading-comprehension benchmarks with imaginary, supported, and contradicting contexts, plus non-affirmative variants.

findings.finding_summary: Mixtral performed near perfectly on supported affirmative items and on the imaginary set, but showed a large decline on contradicting contexts and especially weak performance on non-affirmative items. It was among the models with the biggest drop on negative non-factives and had a very dramatic decrease on modals and conditionals.
findings.measure: SQuAD F1 on supported, contradicting, and imaginary context-question pairs; non-affirmative F1 by semantic condition

findings.finding_summary: On context-faithfulness, Mixtral was described as practically unaffected by parametric knowledge on affirmative and negative contexts, but the issue resurfaced for hypothetical contexts. Prompting strategies improved average accuracy somewhat, but chain-of-thought with instructed prompting negatively impacted some non-affirmative cases.
findings.measure: Relative performance across supported, contradicting, and imaginary sets under different prompts

quality_tier_rationale: This is an empirical benchmark/evaluation paper, but it is not a K-12 instructional intervention study and does not test educational outcomes. The evidence is about general LLM reading-comprehension behavior rather than classroom literacy effectiveness.
impact_tier_rationale: No K-12 reading or literacy instruction impact is measured here, and no effect sizes for educational outcomes are reported. The paper is therefore not evidence of instructional impact in the requested sense.
